# Helping your midwife find you

### A little planning now can make a big difference later

Hello from your Riverside community midwives!

We’re looking forward to welcoming your baby with you. Whether this is your first baby or you’ve done this before, a few small things can help us find your home and get through the door quickly when the time comes.

We like to think of your midwife as part of the family: someone coming to help, reassure and share a very special day. We just might need a little help finding the right house first.

## First things first: when to call

Our home birth cover starts from **37 weeks of pregnancy**. If you think you are in labour before 37 weeks, you will need to go to hospital. Call the Riverside birth line for advice straight away.

From 37 weeks, **call the Riverside birth line when you think labour has started**. Please call the birth line rather than your midwife’s personal mobile. The birth line reaches the midwife who is on call and can help you.

It’s a good idea to save the birth line number in your phone now and keep it somewhere easy to find, such as on the fridge. Your birth partner can save it too.

If you’re not sure whether labour has started, or you’re worried about yourself or your baby, call the birth line for advice. You don’t have to work it all out on your own.

**Riverside birth line:** ______________________________

## Help us find your home

A sat nav is useful, but it doesn’t always tell the whole story. At 3am, in the rain, with a car full of equipment, a few extra directions can be worth their weight in biscuits.

When you call the birth line, tell us anything that will help us find you. For example:

- Is your house number easy to see from the road?
- Does your home have a name instead of a number?
- Is the entrance around the back or down a path?
- Is there a gate, barrier or door entry code we’ll need?
- Does your street look different from the sat nav directions?
- Is there a landmark nearby that will help us?

If your home has a name, please make sure it is easy to see. One midwife looking for a cottage in a row of terraces ended up at a chippy instead. Tempting, but not quite where she needed to be!

If you have what3words, you can give us the three words for the entrance we should use. You can also send a location pin on WhatsApp to the birth line phone. It helps to check that the pin shows the right entrance, especially if you live in a block of flats or on a large estate.

And if you feel like putting balloons on the gate, we won’t complain. One family did this and we found them straight away. A lovely welcome—and a very useful sign!

## If you live in a flat

Flats can be tricky to find, even when we have the right address. Flat 14 isn’t always next to flat 13. Sometimes it’s in a different building altogether!

Please tell us:

- The name or number of your building and which entrance to use.
- Your floor and flat number.
- Any door entry code, or which buzzer to press.
- Whether there is a lift and how to find it.
- Anything else that will help us find your door.

If someone is with you and it’s practical for them to meet us at the entrance, that can help too. One dad once waved a tea towel from a window after a midwife had spent rather too long driving around the block. It worked!

## Let there be light

If it’s dark, please switch on the porch light or any light near your entrance. In winter, dark streets can look very much alike, and a light helps us see your number, gate and path.

If you have outside steps or a path, a light helps us get to you safely while carrying our equipment.

## A little space for our cars

**Two midwives come for the birth**, usually in separate cars. If possible, please leave two parking spaces nearby.

We bring quite a lot with us, including gas and air cylinders, a big bag and sometimes birthing pool equipment. The closer we can park, the easier it is to get everything to you. Our arms will thank you!

If you live in a permit zone, including areas around Anfield and Kensington, please check with the council about a visitor permit. If you have a permit for us to use, have it ready so it can be placed on the dashboard. Please let us know about any parking restrictions when you call.

We know parking isn’t always easy. Just do what you can, and tell us where the best place to park is.

## A clear way in

Please make sure we can get through the front door and along the hallway and stairs as easily as possible. If you can, move shoes, washing baskets, toys and anything else that might be in the way.

Lego has many wonderful qualities. Being stepped on in the dark is not one of them.

If your door is open, please make sure someone is there to show us in, or let us know which door to use. One midwife once walked into the wrong house and was offered a Jammie Dodger by a very nice gentleman. A kind welcome, but not the family she was looking for!

## A little help from your pets

We know pets are part of the family too. But when the midwives arrive, please put pets safely in another room.

Even the friendliest dog can get excited when visitors arrive carrying lots of interesting things. We once knew a lovely staffie called Pippin who gave such an enthusiastic welcome that a midwife nearly dropped the gas and air!

Keeping pets in another room gives everyone a little more space and helps us get to you and your baby safely.

## Thank you

There’s no need for your home to look perfect. We’re not coming to inspect the washing up or judge the toys. We’re coming to care for you and welcome your baby.

A visible address, a light on and a clear way in can make a big difference. And if there’s anything unusual about finding your home, please tell us—we’d much rather hear about it than take the scenic route!

We look forward to seeing you.

**Your Riverside community midwives**

---

# Fridge checklist ✓

### Before the big day

☐ I have saved the **Riverside birth line number** in my phone.

☐ My birth partner or another person supporting me has the number too.

☐ I know that home birth cover starts at **37 weeks**. If I think I’m in labour before then, I’ll call the birth line for advice and will need to go to hospital.

☐ My house number or name is easy to see, or I have extra directions ready.

☐ I have my what3words location or a WhatsApp location pin ready, if useful.

☐ If I live in a flat, I have my building, entrance, floor, flat number and entry details ready.

☐ I have checked parking and visitor permit arrangements, if needed.

### When it’s time

☐ I’ll **call the Riverside birth line**, not my midwife’s personal mobile.

☐ I’ll tell the midwife anything that will help them find my home.

☐ I’ll switch on the porch or entrance light if it’s dark.

☐ I’ll leave space for two cars nearby if possible.

☐ I’ll have any visitor permit ready.

☐ I’ll clear the entrance, hallway and stairs as much as I can.

☐ I’ll ask someone to put pets safely in another room.

**Riverside birth line:** ______________________________
